The (CH3)2NH2CuCl3 crystals were grown using a slow evaporation method.
Alcohol was found to be the best solvent for growing the (CH3)2NH2CuCl3 crystals.
The optimal growth temperature was around 35°C.
The largest crystal grown was 12x7x4 mm in size.
The crystal structure was monoclinic with space group I2/a.
The lattice parameters were a = 11.97 Å, b = 8.6258 Å, c = 14.34 Å, and β = 97.47°.
The magnetic susceptibility showed a Curie-like behavior with no magnetic transition down to 2 K.
The specific heat measurements revealed low-field antiferromagnetic ordering, a field-induced spin gapped state, and a field-induced magnetic ordering state.
The degree of supersaturation of the solution affected the crystal size and quality.
The optimal ratio of raw materials to solvent volume was 1 mmol per 10 ml of alcohol.
The recrystallization process helped overcome the issue of the crystals deliquescing in air.
The X-ray diffraction data indicated single phase and good crystallinity of the obtained crystals.
The magnetic measurements confirmed the absence of magnetic ordering above 2 K.
The specific heat measurements demonstrated the low-temperature magnetic behavior in detail.
The growth conditions were studied for three different solvents: methanol, alcohol, and water.
